title: a librarian node id is its master row number, and a node row is VOID, NOTCACHED or data
intention: trees addresses every node by its master row number only: a node row is in one of three states (void, notcached, data); a write at a row past the local end lays the rows between as NOTCACHED; a slot is reserved from the home box's librarian before the write and stays reserved until the write completes; a voided row is reused; the hash-keyed live rows move to row numbers with nothing dropped.
why: Akien, Q#104, 2026-11-14 (outline 4.3.1.5.1.2): 'there shall be no data node ids based on anything other than master row number ... any other data node lookup method requires a search. row ID does not and is direct.' Measured 2026-11-14: trees.node_id_for is sha256(content)[:16], cairn_nodes.node_id is a text PRIMARY KEY of that hash, there is no state column, and cairn_nodes holds 46014 live rows, cairn_embeddings 28457, cairn_links 7, across 39 leaf tables.
traces_to: Law 1 (a row id is direct, a search re-derives the address every time) and outline 4.3.1.5.1-4.3.1.5.1.4; Law 7 (a node off its three states is a bug, refused loudly).
how: D1 a new node table cairn_node_rows (row_id bigint PRIMARY KEY, state text CHECK in void/notcached/data, the data columns of today's cairn_nodes, nullable unless state='data', plus legacy_id text) beside the old table, which is not altered. D2 reserve/write/void/read in trees: reserve() asks an injected home-reserver (on the home box, CAIRN_HOME_HOST unset, it is local: lowest VOID row, else max+1, laid as NOTCACHED); write(row, data) lays rows local_max+1..row-1 as NOTCACHED, then the row as data; void(row) clears data to VOID; read(row) returns the row, and a NOTCACHED row is fed through an injected master-fetch when one is given. D3 deposit/deposit_keyed reserve a row and return it as node_id (an int); duplicate-content detection goes through a keyed index tree librarian_content_index (key = sha256 of content -> row), a tree lookup, not a node search (Q#109 asks whether this stands). node_id_for is deleted. Embedding, leaf and link rows carry node_row bigint; their own ids stay as they are pending Q#108. D4 migrate_to_row_ids.py in the trees tool: dry run by default, --write applies; never drops or alters an existing row. D5 the red-first proof, over scratch tables only.

clauses.claim: deposit into a scratch leaf returns an integer node_id equal to the row it wrote, and reading that row returns state data with the content; no sha256 id appears in the node row or the return

a write at row 123 into a node list whose last row is 12 lays rows 13..122 as NOTCACHED and row 123 as data, and a read of row 50 with a master-fetch given returns the master's data and leaves row 50 as data locally
void(row) leaves the row VOID with its data cleared, and the next reserve on the home box hands that row back before any new row
on a remote box (CAIRN_HOME_HOST set) reserve asks the injected home-reserver and never mints a row itself; with no reserver given it refuses, naming the home host, and nothing lands
a row whose state is not one of void/notcached/data, or a data row with no content, is refused by the table (CHECK) and by the write door, naming the state
the same content deposited twice, into two trees, lands one node row (found through librarian_content_index) and two leaves, and the second deposit appends an attestation

migrate_to_row_ids over a scratch copy of hash-keyed nodes, embeddings, a vectored leaf, a keyed leaf and links: the dry run writes nothing; --write lays one data row per old node in created order, maps every legacy id, fills node_row on every embedding, leaf and link, drops and deletes nothing (old row counts unchanged), and a second --write changes nothing

decisions.text: D1+D2+D3: cairn_node_rows, the three states, reserve/write/void/read with injected home-reserver and master-fetch, deposit returning the row, the content index tree, node_id_for deleted, node_row on embeddings/leaves/links.
D4: the additive migration, dry run by default, idempotent, never drops or alters an existing row; prints per-table before/after counts and exits 1 on any unmapped row.
D5: the red-first proof, one tooth per clause, over store.scratch tables only.

out: running the migration over live (a separate act after PROVED, dry run first, Akien's 46014 rows)

measured.saw: node_id_for = sha256(content)[:16]; cairn_nodes.node_id text PRIMARY KEY; no state column
cairn_nodes 46014, cairn_embeddings 28457, cairn_links 7, cairn_threads 0, 39 tables with leaf_id, 43 node_id/source_id/target_id columns
measured.how: read-only SELECT count(*) through store.query on the live db
